svg.title: The Spotify schema: Users, Songs, and Listens, joined by two foreign keys
svg.desc: Three tables shown together. Users has a primary key user_id; Songs has a primary key song_id; Listens has a primary key listen_id and two foreign keys, user_id pointing at Users.user_id and song_id pointing at Songs.song_id. One row is decoded: listen 1 means Mickey (user 1) played Evermore (song 1) and rated it 4.5. Color key: blue PK and FK badges mark the keys, per-user identity bars color the rows by user.
svg.text: One schema: three tables, two keys tie them together
Every query in the course is a question over these. The IDs are how they connect.

g.text: user_id is one unique value per user,
like a student ID or a social security
number. No two users share it.
user_id and song_id are foreign keys.
Each must match a real id in Users or
Songs, so a listen can't point at nobody.
